assumptions.pricing_model: Black-76 on synthetic forward derived from call-put parity F=K+exp(rT)*(C-P)
assumptions.dividend_or_carry_handling: Embedded in the synthetic forward; no separate dividend yield assumed
assumptions.gamma_unit: rupees per one index-point squared per lot; standard gamma coefficient, before the 0.5 Taylor factor
assumptions.theta_unit: rupees per calendar day per lot
assumptions.position: short one call plus short one put at the fixed strike
assumptions.entry_iv: simple mean of independently solved call and put Black-76 IVs
assumptions.book_snapshot: At every executed entry timestamp, all positions still open are repriced from that minute's call/put prices and spot; exposures are summed after including the new entry
assumptions.sanity_check: Because theta is reported daily, |theta/gamma| is multiplied by 365 before comparison with 0.5*IV^2*F^2; rate terms cause expected residual error
assumptions.rule_b: Fractional research weights min(1, median ratio / trade ratio); this is not integer-lot executable

limitations: Option and spot observations are one-minute values, not ticks.
No historical bid/ask quotes are available, so IV and Greeks use recorded option prices without spread modelling.
Black-76 uses a synthetic forward derived from same-strike call-put parity because a matched futures series was not supplied.
Some tercile/quintile, route, month and tail-day subsets are small; their Sharpe and stop rates are unstable.
Rule A and Rule B full-sample results are in-sample. The leave-one-month-out filter is the less-biased filter estimate.
Greeks are model estimates and do not include discrete strike-surface interpolation or intraminute movement.
Book-level analysis stops rather than imputes at 5 entry timestamps (6 position-minute prices missing); those book ratios are blank and excluded.
